recipes.name: Easy and Quick Halushki
ingredients_raw: salt and ground black pepper to taste

steps.text: Snip bacon into small pieces with a scissors and cook in a large skillet over medium heat until crisp, stirring often, about 10 minutes. Cook and stir onion with bacon until translucent, about 5 more minutes; set bacon and onion aside, leaving drippings in the skillet.
Bring a large pot of lightly salted water to a boil. Cook egg noodles in the boiling water, stirring occasionally until cooked through but firm to the bite, about 5 minutes. Drain.

Transfer bacon and onion mixture with drippings into the pot used to cook the noodles and cook and stir cabbage until coated with drippings. Cover pot and cook until cabbage is tender, 10 to 12 minutes, stirring occasionally. Gently stir in noodles and season to taste with salt and black pepper.

raw_recipe.headline: Easy and Quick Halushki
raw_recipe.description: You can make haluski, a comforting, hearty dish of bacon, egg noodles and cabbage, with only five ingredients in about half an hour.

video.description: A Polish noodle comfort food that is traditional, tasty, and simple. Easy to add extra seasonings or make as is!

review.reviewBody: I make halushki (cabbage and noodles) all the time, but usually use turkey kielbasa in place of the bacon and add a bit of butter at the end of cooking right before serving. Today, Italy met Poland when I subbed Johnsonville® mild ground Italian sausage for the bacon. Delish! I still added 2 TBS of butter to finish. Yum. Don't forget to use LOTS of fresh ground black pepper!

Per another reviewers suggestion, I used one pot, stirring the cabbage into the bacon & onions mixture. Per another reviewers suggestion, I added caraway seed - brilliant! I also added garlic. My Italian/Irish husband added Parmesan, and I have to admit it was a great enhancement.

I make Haluski frequently and I use a large disposable tin pan, chop up a pound of thin sliced bacon, spread out in the tin pan, bake at 400° until crisp(not burned) take the bacon out, do not drain, add chopped onions to the grease, bake until translucent, add the chopped up head of cabbage to the same pan, stir and bake until cabbage is soft, not mushy, add a pound of el dente lightly buttered egg noodles, stir, add pepper to taste and serve. It comes out delicious and clean up is a breeze.

I had made some extra wide noodles last week and had some leftover. This was Delish and went perfect with my pork roast! I cooked the bacon, sliced the onions and threw those in. Once they were wilted, I tossed in 1/2 a head of shredded Napa cabbage and sauteed a few more minutes. I did add some celery seed for a little contrast. Next time I would like to try caraway seed instead. Thank you lburger24.

This was pretty good. My daughter (a bacon fanatic) loved it. I remember eating "halushka" once at a heritage day at my old church. One of the couples there were both from Poland. He was born there but was brought to America as an infant. She grew up there, only leaving when she met her husband while he was visiting his grandparents. She prepared halushka, pierogi, and some type of delicious meatballs. Her halushka did not have bacon in it. Instead, she sauteed onions, leeks, and garlic with the cabbage in clarified butter. Then, she added stock or water with the egg noodles and cooked it until the noodles were done and the water or stock was reduced. She then, just before serving or even at the table, stirred in sour cream.

This is how she shared her recipe and it took me several tries until it tasted like hers. Maybe no bacon since it was served with meat? It is, though, the best kind of comfort food.

I made this dish and it was delicious! I sauteed the onion, bacon in the butter until onions were translucent and bacon was just starting to crisp, then added the cabbage and cooked it all together until cabbage was very wilted and cooked done. I added more butter when I added the cabbage. After I drained the noodles, I added all the incredients in the stockpot and it came out great! Of course, it's not a heart-healthy dish since you are using bacon grease and butter for seasoning, but still yummy! I will make again.

Recipe Group: I wasn't sure how I'd like this recipe, but ended up really loving it. Will definitely make again. Next time, though, I'll use only 1/2 or 3/4 lb of noodles, as it made a huge amount of food and I thought it would be better with less noodles anyway. I followed the ingredients but slightly changed the cooking method just a bit. I cooked the bacon, then drained the pan, reserving the drippings which I used as needed to cook the onions & then the cabbage, instead of using the entire amount. When I stirred in the noodles, I added a few more spoonfuls of bacon drippings for some additional flavor. There was still a fair amount of leftover drippings, and it still tasted fabulous, so I'm glad I didn't use the whole amount as I think it would have been too greasy, and we certainly saved a lot of fat calories. Husband wants to try it with kielbasa instead of bacon, and I agree it would be tasty that way as well.

I've given this dish a five star mainly because it has been a go to dish around the world for all the years of my life, my mother and grandmother made it before I existed and I'm 81, my mother often made it during the WW11 years, at that time she used any meat we happened to have leftover. I have made it with bacon, kielbasa, corned beef, sausage and without meat. I use the full head of cabbage, I usually use egg noodles and kielbasa and one onion, after I add the hot noodles I add 4 TBS butter, mix well, add pepper to taste and serve. I love garlic but for some reason I don't add it to this dish, I don't think my mother did either, it's just not traditional to the recipe.

5+++. Excellent, easy meal the whole family, including kids, loves. This brought back such good memories! It was a staple on the table of my German great aunts & my nearly daily dinner as a financially strapped, newly iindependent 20 something. In true depression era frugality, my aunts taught me to keep a jar of ham & bacon drippings handy to make this when no meat was available. Serve with black caraway bread. Thank you for reminding me of this scrumptious dish. :-)

Add rinse and drained sourkraut when cooking then when done add stick of butter or oleo. Wonderful
good old fashion Halushki

I did step 3 in reverse. After sautéing the bacon and onion (plus I added 1/2c celery and 2 TBLS diced garlic) instead of transferring the bacon/cabbage to the pasta pot, I added the pasta to the cabbage mix. You need a large, deep sauté pan to do this but I think it turned out better this way. I think you need to season with S&P throughout the cabbage sauté process. This was good but needed more flavor for my preference. Glad I tried. Thanks Laura!
As is, the recipe is great! I like to change it up depending on what I have left over in the fridge. Kielbasa, bacon, and a tablespoon of cottage cheese at the end.
I followed the recipe exactly and it was so good! I'm definitely making it again.

I made this for the first time this past weekend. It turned out great. After reading reviews I decided to tweak it by using only 3 tablespoons of butter. I also fried 6 slices of bacon and sautéed onion, red, yellow, orange and green peppers with the cabbage. I also added sliced chicken sausage that I browned first. I will definitely make this again!!! So tasty 😋! Thanks for a great recipe.
I have had Halushki for many years and my Auntie used homemade noodles and that was amazing and great.

My mother-in-law was Slovak and she made this dish. Simplest récipé in ingredients, bursting with a full, delicious flavor. (She made hers the Slovak way with tiny little homemade grated potato dumplings - all day cooking! But use good noodles, and this is also just the best. I’ve also heard of using spætzle.). Even people that “don’t like” cabbage will love this, because the bacon is the prevailing flavor. It’s just pure deliciousness! I cook this for my nephew.

We love this dish, and have been making it for decades. If I have to stretch ( often have drop in guests) I will add a diced carrot or two and a few sliced up celery stalks but the key is the caraway seeds! Great with a salad or fresh crusty bread.

I have had versions of this before and this was by far the easiest and most flavorful. I did use the turkey sausage instead of the bacon as I cannot eat pork these days :(. All day my husband said he wouldn't like it and tried to get me to make something else. Once he tried it, he loved it and went back for a second helping. This is definitely a keeper!
I used eggless noodles and a pound soy bacon. It turned out great.
